This page of the Apple Product Environmental Report for the iMac, with a date introduced of October 28, 2024, outlines several key environmental and material highlights. 

Under the section "Progress toward our 2030 goal", the report lists "More than 15% recycled content" and "Over 20% of manufacturing electricity sourced from renewable energy". 

The "Packaging" section states that it is "100% fiber-based, due to our work to remove plastic in packaging" and "100% recycled or responsibly sourced wood fibers". 

The "Supplier Code of Conduct" section notes that through the Apple Supplier Code of Conduct, strict standards are set for safeguarding people and the environment in the supply chain. 

Regarding "Smarter chemistry", the iMac includes arsenic-free glass, mercury-free, brominated flame retardant-free, and PVC-free components. 

The "Longevity" section mentions that the iMac was assessed in the Reliability Testing Lab using rigorous testing methods that simulate customers' experiences. 

The "Recovery" section notes that devices can be returned through Apple Trade In at a retail store or online to get a new life or be recycled for free. 

A prominent statement declares that "iMac uses 100% recycled aluminum in the stand". 

The bottom includes an Energy Star logo with the text "ENERGY STAR" and an EPEAT Gold logo labeled "epeat GOLD 6".

This page from the Apple iMac Product Environmental Report is titled Progress toward carbon neutral. It describes emissions reductions for iMac (two ports) with 256GB. The text notes that emissions have been reduced by more than 20 percent against a business-as-usual scenario, with 15 percent recycled content including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand, reducing total product emissions by about 13 percent. Suppliers working toward 100 percent low-carbon electricity have reduced product emissions by 5 percent.

The page features a vertical bar chart detailing carbon emissions in kilograms. The first bar has a total of 445 kg labeled Baseline emissions7, consisting of segments for Materials and process emissions, Electricity for manufacturing, Electricity for product use, and Transportation. The second bar is labeled Emissions reductions with a total of -99 kg, showing segments for Recycled and low-carbon materials8, Materials and process emissions, Low-carbon electricity9, Electricity for manufacturing, Electricity for product use, Non-air shipping, and Transportation. The third bar has a total of 346 kg labeled iMac emissions10, comprising segments for Materials and process emissions, Electricity for manufacturing, Electricity for product use, Transportation, and Renewable energy emissions11. The arithmetic relationship shown is baseline emissions of 445 kg minus emissions reductions of -99 kg resulting in iMac emissions of 346 kg.

This page from Apple's iMac Product Environmental Report is titled "Taking responsibility for our products at every stage". The introductory text states that Apple takes responsibility for products throughout their life cycles, focusing on reducing climate change impact, conserving resources, and using safer materials. A subheading reads, "We sell millions of products. So making even small adjustments can have a meaningful impact."

The page features a circular diagram illustrating Apple's lifecycle stages with green icons and arrows pointing clockwise. At the top, the first icon shows three recycling arrows, with text reading "DESIGN AND SOURCE" and "Maximize the use of recycled content and responsibly source primary materials". Moving clockwise, the second icon shows a solar panel and sun, with text reading "MAKE" and "Uphold high standards of labor and human rights, health and safety, and minimizing our environmental impact". The third icon displays a globe, accompanied by text reading "PACKAGE AND SHIP" and "Remove plastic from our packaging and minimize emissions from transportation". The fourth icon shows a plug, with text reading "USE" and "Minimize emissions from product use, enhance product longevity, and seek to avoid exposure to harmful chemicals". Finally, the fifth icon shows a recycling leaf symbol, with text reading "RECOVER" and "Reuse products through Apple Trade In and maximize material recovery at end of life". The footer reads "iMac | Product Environmental Report" on the left and "3" on the right.

This page of the Apple iMac Product Environmental Report is titled Design and Source. The top section features a circular diagram with arrows pointing clockwise, labeled with the text DESIGN AND SOURCE at the top, MAKE on the right, PACKAGE AND SHIP at the bottom right, USE at the bottom left, and RECOVER on the top left. Green icons accompany each label. Text states that iMac contains more than 15 percent recycled content. By 2025, Apple plans to use 100 percent recycled cobalt in all Apple-designed batteries, 100 percent recycled tin soldering, 100 percent recycled gold plating in all Apple-designed rigid and flexible printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. 

Below, six circular material samples with accompanying text describe recycled content usage. Aluminum text states: We use 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand. Copper text states: We use 100 percent recycled copper in multiple printed circuit boards. We also use 100 percent recycled copper in multiple thermal module components. Gold text states: We use 100 percent recycled gold in the plating of multiple printed circuit boards. Plastic text states: We use at least 50 percent recycled plastic in 13 components. Rare earth elements text states: We use 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, representing 99 percent of the total rare earth elements in the device. Tin text states: We use 100 percent recycled tin in the solder of multiple printed circuit boards. 

A final section titled Smarter chemistry describes chemical safety. Text states that iMac is free of harmful substances like brominated flame retardants, PVC, phthalates, arsenic in the glass, and mercury. And 100 percent of the materials in iMac are covered by our Regulated Substances Specification. We go beyond what’s required by aiming to understand the non-regulated substances in every part of every product—an effort that requires an industry-leading level of transparency through the entire supply chain. We consistently identify the makeup of over 80 percent by mass of iMac devices. Page number 4 is at the bottom right, and iMac Product Environmental Report is at the bottom left.

It features a circular lifecycle diagram on the upper left showing five stages with the attached text "DESIGN AND SOURCE", "MAKE", "PACKAGE AND SHIP", "USE", and "RECOVER". Below the title, the text explains that the Apple Supplier Code of Conduct sets strict standards for safeguarding people and the environment, noting that over 20 percent of manufacturing electricity is sourced from supplier low-carbon energy projects, supported by Apple's Supplier Clean Energy Program.2

This page from the Apple iMac Product Environmental Report is titled "Package and Ship". It features a circular lifecycle diagram showing five stages with icons and labels: design and source, make, package and ship, use, and recover, with the "package and ship" stage highlighted in green. Text explains that iMac packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and contains no plastic except for inks, coatings, and adhesives, marking a milestone toward removing plastics from packaging by 2025. It adds that efforts include improving packaging, increasing recycled content, and reducing volume, while responsibly managed forests cover all new wood fiber used. Additionally, less carbon-intensive shipping modes like rail and ocean are prioritized over air transport.

On the left side, three statistics are listed with green accent lines: 100% of the packaging is fiber-based, due to work to remove plastic in packaging; 76% recycled content in fiber packaging; and 100% of the virgin wood fiber in the packaging is responsibly sourced. On the right, an illustration shows the boxed iMac. At the bottom left, the text reads "iMac | Product Environmental Report", and at the bottom right is the page number 6.

Below, it states that iMac uses 58 percent less energy than the requirement for ENERGY STAR.18 Body text explains Apple’s energy-efficient design, software, power-efficient components, testing labs, software updates, repairs through Apple Authorized Service Providers (AASPs), low-carbon energy projects, and grid decarbonization. 

A subsection titled "Energy consumption of ENERGY STAR-rated products" notes that Apple devices consistently rank among high-performing products rated by ENERGY STAR, which sets specifications reflecting the 25 percent most energy-efficient devices on the market. It repeats that iMac consumes 58 percent less energy than the requirement for ENERGY STAR.18 

Further down, two sections appear side by side. "Designed to last" states that iMac features a durable unibody construction and rigorous durability testing. "Made with smarter chemistry" explains that Apple applies rigorous controls for materials users touch based on recommendations from toxicologists and dermatologists.
